title: Diesel Unsold

source.title: Russia's land gains in Ukraine dwindle as its diesel reportedly goes unsold
source.note: published 11-06 18:23 (page time; last updated 18:39); the 11-06 sweep matched it on 'diesel'. Read in full on 11-07 via the cloud fetch (complete, 29 body paragraphs, one subhead 'The oil war' before ¶21) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. Twenty paragraphs of battlefield and nine of the deal: the dek pairs them. Chosen as the newest row on H1 itself — the deal's cargo — the first page in the queue to carry the deal since 10-24; the AP wire on the same cargo (PBS NewsHour, 11-05: two hulls turned, a third 'for orders') is the primary and sits in the queue on the npr-pbs ruling; my call

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the cargo itself, read from the LI corner outside the US horizon on the day the first hull was due in New York (Kpler, 10-23: due 11-07). Per the FT, as the page carries it: the Kremlin loaded four tankers with diesel hoping to sell to the US and 'effectively end sanctions', and they have failed to find buyers willing to risk the legal consequences; the Kremlin calls the report fake news. The deal sized as 1.8 million tonnes by year-end 'to the global market' (the holder's schedule summed: 300,000 + 500,000 + 1,000,000); the invitation set against the Lindsey Graham Act signed eleven days before it; Blumenthal's 27 October warning to a Greek operator of one of the four not to offload in the US — 'only Congress can make it legally valid'; Ukraine's eight refineries in seven days 'designed to scupper' the deal. The pump, the price, the Strait and the holder's own words are not on the page

zAxis.pos: the cargo lands and the deal delivers — diesel into the US, prices down by it
zAxis.neg: it does not — four hulls loaded, no buyer, the statute and the licence in a tangle, the refineries that make the cargo hit

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) and the schedule restated 10-24 (300,000 t immediately · 500,000 t November · 1,000,000 t after · 3,000,000 t more). On this page the delivery is read on its due date from outside the US horizon: the cargo exists (four hulls loaded), the buyer does not (the FT), and the gate is legal, not physical — the Act, the licence, a senator's letter to a shipper. The page's vehicle is Russia's war going badly: the diesel unsold is set beside land gains of 0.38 sq km a day as two readings of one weakness. The deal's own terms (300,000 t 'immediately') are not restated; 1.8 million is the sum. Nothing on the page says what the diesel was for

lines.quote: Russia's land gains dwindle as its diesel 'reportedly goes unsold'; US traders 'reportedly refuse to honour' Trump's diesel deal with Putin
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek): the deal named with both holders' names on it and the cargo unsold — 'reportedly' twice; 'honour' the vehicle; 'US traders' appear in the dek and nowhere in the body (the body says buyers unwilling to risk the legal consequences)
lines.zWhy: a cargo reportedly unsold is the delivery not shown

lines.quote: Russian forces took 117.38 sq km in the first ten months of 2026 (ISW) against 5,304 sq km in 2025 and 3,604 in 2024 — 0.38 sq km a day this year
lines.note: the battlefield as the record — right domain (Russia's weakness), wrong plane (the land, not the cargo); four paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: land gains read neither way on the cargo

lines.quote: 381,300 Russian personnel killed or seriously wounded 1 January – 31 October (Ukraine's General Staff; Al Jazeera cannot verify); 54,400 in October; recruitment 24,000–30,000 a month
lines.note: casualties — the vehicle's second half; the one hedge on the page is the publication's own
lines.zWhy: casualties read neither way on the cargo

lines.quote: Zelenskyy: the worsening trends are why Russia intensifies long-range strikes on energy; 2,346 drones and more than 80 missiles in the week to 6 November; 'psychological warfare'; blackouts at the start of winter
lines.note: the energy war from the other side — Ukraine's blackouts, not Russia's diesel; four paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: strikes on Ukraine's energy read neither way on the cargo

lines.quote: at least 50 killed at Komyshuvakha on an aid day (GUR: 'the invaders knew'); the six-day Oleshky ceasefire brokered by the First Lady ended that day — 800 evacuated, 17 buses for Ukraine against four for Russia; the reporter who said so arrested
lines.note: object-shaped things off the object — a dated localised ceasefire with a delivery (800 evacuated) sorts to the register's intake; six paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a localised ceasefire reads neither way on the cargo

lines.quote: eight refineries in seven days: three on 30 October (Novak), two in the Ufa complex on the 31st, Lukoil's Nizhny Novgorod on 1 November, a Samara dispatch station on the 2nd, Yaroslavl on the 3rd, Ryazan on the 5th
lines.note: THE SUPPLY SIDE DATED: the refineries that make the cargo, hit by name and day — the page's most fluid line on the object
lines.zWhy: refineries hit eight in seven days is the deal's supply narrowed

lines.quote: the strikes designed to deprive Russia of revenue and to 'scupper' the 9 October Putin–Trump deal, in which the US leader invited Russia to sell 1.8 million tonnes of diesel to the global market by year-end to help bring down transport prices
lines.note: THE DEAL NAMED AND SIZED from outside the US horizon: 1.8 million tonnes is the holder's 10-24 schedule summed (300,000 + 500,000 + 1,000,000), and 'to the global market' is not 'to the US'; 'scupper' the vehicle — the strikes read as aimed at the deal
lines.zWhy: strikes designed to scupper the deal is the delivery contested at its source

lines.quote: the invitation went against US oil sanctions and the Lindsey Graham Act the president had signed eleven days earlier, which gave him the power to sanction countries buying Russian oil
lines.note: THE GATE: the statute dated against the deal — signed eleven days before the invitation (28 September by this count); the Act's own waiver (fox 10-23) is not on the page
lines.zWhy: an invitation against a statute signed eleven days earlier is the delivery's legal gate

lines.quote: per the FT: the Kremlin has loaded four tankers with diesel hoping to sell to the US and 'effectively end sanctions'; they have failed to find buyers willing to risk the legal consequences
lines.note: THE CARGO UNSOLD, on the day the first hull was due in New York (Kpler, 10-23): four hulls loaded, no buyer; the FT the source, the hulls unnamed here (the AP wire names two — Talisman, Leruo — turned toward Brazil and the Mediterranean)
lines.zWhy: four loaded hulls without a buyer on the due date is the delivery not shown

lines.quote: the FT report is fake news
lines.note: constitutive — the deal's other party on the cargo: a denial, no hull, no buyer, no port. Not Dia-scored (the AP wire has Peskov's fuller form the same day: 'all the diesel will find its buyers', and Dmitriev's 'Fake. Tankers destined for the US continue on course')

lines.quote: 27 October: Blumenthal, the Act's co-author, warned a Greek shipping company operating one of the four diesel-laden ships not to offload its cargo in the US
lines.note: THE LETTER: a dated record line — a senator to a shipper, the hull's operator named by nationality only; the primary (the letter) owed
lines.zWhy: a senator's warning to the hull's operator is the delivery blocked at the pier

lines.quote: the president may have licensed the transaction, but 'only Congress can make it legally valid' — read as a warning to every shipper of a tangle between statute and executive order
lines.note: the licence against the statute: the author generalises one letter to every hull — the page's one challenge predicate; 'tangle' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a licence only Congress can validate is the delivery's gate read as closed

lines.quote: US courts have struck down many of the president's executive orders in his first two years
lines.note: the close: the licence's durability read by the courts' record — a frame, undated, no order named
lines.zWhy: orders struck down before reads the licence as fragile
